newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian debt market eyes weakening crown.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian debt market eyes weakening crown.

text.p: 1400 GMT -- The Norwegian debt market was largely unchanged with eyes fixed on the weakening crown, which continued to slip as foreign investors led a sell-off of the petrocurrency, analysts and dealers said.

Analysts speculated lower oil prices, wage talks later this month and high Norwegian CPI figures in the recent past had prompted some investors to sell. Investors may also have thought the crown would not strengthen any further and had reached its potential, they said.
Resistance seen at 4.1720 crowns against the mark, but analysts saw fundamentals leading to a stronger crown over time.

At 1400 GMT, the crown stood at 4.1270 against the mark, down from 4.1030 at the same time on Thursday. The crown was quoted at 101.26 against the inverse ECU index for a four-month low against the basket of European currencies.
* 2007 bond yield two points lower at 6.14 pct
* Norway over Bunds gap one point narrower at 33 points
* Three-month eurokrone six points higher at 3.55 pct
